_: One example of each payload in the native LiveState contract (NATIVE-SHARED, 'The contracts'). The Swift structs in ios/App/Shared/ decode this file; the JavaScript side produces it. Whoever changes one side runs both checks against this file. Field spellings here ARE the wire format: camelCase, no renames.

liveStatePaused._: The session paused from the phone, or restored at boot from a draft the process died in. Sent with phase 'paused' and pausedAt (ISO 8601, when the pause began); rest is null; everything else keeps describing where it stopped. On resume the engine shifts startedAt forward by the length of the pause and sends an ordinary work/rest state. Both additions are optional so an older shell still decodes.
liveStatePaused.title: Kettlebell Circuit

liveStateMinimal._: AMRAP round: no set position, no target, bodyweight, nothing after it.
liveStateMinimal.title: Ten Minute Core

liveStateUnknownPhase._: A phase this build of the shell has never heard of. Must decode, not throw: the web app ships independently of the native shell.
liveStateUnknownPhase.title: Kettlebell Circuit

widgetSummarySignedOut._: What the app publishes on sign-out so the widgets can clear. Every field but v and updatedAt is absent, and it still has to decode.

liveActionWatch._: A set logged from the wrist after the Crown moved: reps and weight are present ONLY when a dial was turned, and app.ts falls back to its own prefill otherwise.

liveActionDial._: The same from the Live Activity's own dial (expanded island / Lock Screen). The ± presses themselves never cross the bridge; this is the one message the dial produces, and only Log set sends it.

liveStateComplex._: A complex mid-round: the counter and the cap the phone's own screen draws. cap/held are ms like rest.total/rest.held; until is the epoch deadline the cap counts down to, 0 until the clock is started; move is the movement the round is up to and is also `exercise`.
liveStateComplex.title: Kettlebell Complex

liveActionRound._: Round N done, from the card. The engine counts a round of the complex on screen and starts the cap if it is not running.

liveActionMark._: The movement the round is up to, ticked from the card. The last tick of a round counts the round, as on the phone.
